methods.label: Reveal a nonnegative square
methods.explanation:
Completing the square makes the least possible value visible. Since \((x+1)^2=x^2+2x+1\), rewrite the function as
\[
y=2\bigl((x+1)^2-1\bigr)+3
=2(x+1)^2+1.
\]
For every real \(x\), the square \((x+1)^2\) is nonnegative, so \(y\ge1\). Equality holds exactly when \(x+1=0\), or \(x=-1\).

Thus the graph has its lowest point at \((-1,1)\), choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
